title: Crestline Fleet Account Road Hazard Program Credit
content:
Roadside allowances granted on a business's Road Hazard Protection certificates earn its Crestline Fleet Account a road hazard program credit, added to the pricing correction on a tire invoice posted with no fleet discount.

| Roadside allowances granted on the business's road hazard certificates less than twenty-four whole months before today | Road hazard program credit |
|---|---|
| eight or more | 15.00 |
| four to seven | 7.50 |
| fewer than four | nothing |

The allowances are read from the Road Hazard Protection records of the business: each entry recording a roadside allowance granted on one of its certificates, dated less than twenty-four whole months before today.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical counts)

| Allowances granted in the period | Credit |
|---|---|
| 3 | none |
| 4 | 7.50 |
| 7 | 7.50 |
| 8 | 15.00 |

## Where the amount sits

Because a fleet invoice posted without the program discount is Crestline's billing error, make-good amounts are added to the pricing correction on a tire invoice that an account invoiced without sales tax received with no fleet discount at all. The correction starts from the restored discount (the fleet discount the ticket should have carried less the discount the invoice already carried). The limit of the invoice amount less the credit memos and early-pay discounts already on the invoice is applied last, after every make-good amount, and prevails over every other part of the correction rule, so a correction can fall below the restored discount only when that limit is lower; the correction is rounded half up to the cent once, after the limit.
